# Implementing Appwrite authentication in NestJS (2025-08-15 18:02Z)

_**User (2025-08-15 05:31Z)**_

Backend (NestJS) notes
- Install appwrite server SDK:
- Flow:
  - Frontend sends JWT (from account.createJWT()) to backend (e.g. /api/auth/session),
    or frontend sends Authorization: Bearer <jwt> on API requests.
  - Backend Guard reads the Bearer token, sets it on Appwrite client: client.setJWT(jwt)
    and then calls account.get() to validate and fetch the user object.
  - If valid, attach user to request and allow the route; otherwise reject.

```typescript name=src/auth/appwrite-auth.guard.ts
import { CanActivate, ExecutionContext, Injectable, UnauthorizedException } from "@nestjs/common";
import { Client, Account } from "appwrite";
import { Request } from "express";

@Injectable()
export class AppwriteAuthGuard implements CanActivate {
  private client = new Client()
    .setEndpoint(process.env.APPWRITE_ENDPOINT || "")
    .setProject(process.env.APPWRITE_PROJECT || "")
    .setKey(process.env.APPWRITE_API_KEY || "");
  private account = new Account(this.client);

  async canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean> {
    const req = context.switchToHttp().getRequest<Request>();

    // 1) Accept Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
    const auth = req.headers["authorization"] || "";
    let token = "";
    if (typeof auth === "string" && auth.startsWith("Bearer ")) {
      token = auth.slice("Bearer ".length);
    }

    // 2) Fallback: accept JWT sent in body (for session endpoint) or cookie named "appwrite_jwt"
    if (!token) {
      token = (req as any).body?.jwt || (req.cookies && req.cookies["appwrite_jwt"]);
    }

    if (!token) {
      throw new UnauthorizedException("No JWT provided");
    }

    try {
      // Set JWT to perform a user.get (this validates token)
      this.client.setJWT(token);
      const user = await this.account.get();

      // attach user to request for controllers to use
      (req as any).user = user;
      return true;
    } catch (err) {
      // token invalid or expired
      throw new UnauthorizedException("Invalid Appwrite JWT");
    } finally {
      // Important: clear JWT from client (so it is not reused cross-request)
      this.client.setJWT("");
    }
  }
}
```

```typescript name=src/auth/auth.controller.ts
import { Controller, Post, Req, Res, UseGuards } from "@nestjs/common";
import { Request, Response } from "express";
import { AppwriteAuthGuard } from "./appwrite-auth.guard";

/**
 * A tiny controller to accept the frontend POST /api/auth/session with { jwt }
 * If valid, we set a server cookie (optional) and return user info.
 *
 * Note: If you prefer not to set your own cookie, you can just rely on the frontend to
 * attach the Bearer token on each request and use the Guard to verify.
 */
@Controller("api/auth")
export class AuthController {
  @Post("session")
  async createSession(@Req() req: Request, @Res() res: Response) {
    const jwt = (req as any).body?.jwt;
    if (!jwt) {
      return res.status(400).json({ error: "jwt required" });
    }

    // Option A: verify token and set server cookie for subsequent requests
    // We will call Appwrite to validate the token by using the Guard pattern manually
    // For demo simplicity we instantiate account client here (alternatively reuse a service).
    const { Client, Account } = require("appwrite");
    const client = new Client()
      .setEndpoint(process.env.APPWRITE_ENDPOINT || "")
      .setProject(process.env.APPWRITE_PROJECT || "")
      .setKey(process.env.APPWRITE_API_KEY || "");
    client.setJWT(jwt);
    const account = new Account(client);

    try {
      const user = await account.get();

      // Set an HttpOnly cookie if you want backend-managed sessions
      // Note: name differs from Appwrite's internal cookie; choose your own
      res.cookie("appwrite_jwt", jwt, {
        httpOnly: true,
        sameSite: "lax",
        secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production",
        maxAge: 1000 * 60 * 60, // 1 hour (jwt lifetime may be shorter)
      });

      return res.json({ user });
    } catch (err) {
      return res.status(401).json({ error: "Invalid JWT" });
    }
  }

  // Example protected route:
  @UseGuards(AppwriteAuthGuard)
  @Post("userinfo")
  async userInfo(@Req() req: Request) {
    return { user: (req as any).user };
  }
}
```

Notes and gotchas
- Redirect URLs: ensure the callback URL you pass to createOAuth2Session is added to the Appwrite OAuth provider allowed redirect URLs.
- Cookie vs header:
  - If you want the browser to automatically send Appwrite's session cookie, frontend and Appwrite must be in compatible domains and CORS/cookie policies must allow it.
  - Alternatively the frontend can call account.createJWT() and send that JWT as Authorization: Bearer <jwt> with each request. On the backend, verify as shown.
- Security:
  - Only use the server-side API key (APPWRITE_API_KEY) on the backend — never expose it to the client.
  - JWTs are short-lived; validate and refresh as needed.
- CORS: allow your frontend origin in Appwrite Console and configure your backend CORS for fetch calls.
